calls.head: Power vs. power
calls.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Konecny’s line (Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Canucks’ first line is DeBrusk, Chytil and Boeser.
calls.call: The Flyers’ L1 (Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny) spends at least 48% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ first line, against about 39% with no line matching.

calls.title: Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny barely saw the Canucks’ first line
calls.plain: Philadelphia sent Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny out against the Canucks’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Tocchet sent them out against O'Connor, Mueller and Karlsson (2:55 of 10:13 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Rick Tocchet would send Foerster, Dvorak and Konecny out against the Canucks’ first line again

calls.head: Expect a grind
calls.body: The Canucks play some of the league’s slowest games, and so do the Flyers. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia a 72% chance, and they delivered.

VAN.head: We gave Vancouver only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Vancouver brought the hits
surprises.body: Vancouver usually hits more than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 215 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 110 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Konecny has a goal and an assist as the Flyers beat the Canucks
paras: Tyson Foerster struck first for the Flyers on the power play early in the first. The Canucks’ Filip Chytil left early in the second period and didn’t return. Noah Cates made it 2-0 for the Flyers early in the period, and Porter Martone stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the period. Filip Hronek got the Canucks on the board a minute and a half later. Vancouver had a goal taken off for goalie interference midway through the second. Jake DeBrusk cut Philadelphia’s lead to 3-2 early in the third, but that was as close as they got. Travis Konecny extended the lead to 4-2 on the power play less than four minutes later. Sean Couturier added an empty-net goal with less than two minutes left to make it 5-2.
The Flyers had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Canucks 29-20. Dan Vladař made 18 saves for the Flyers, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 24 of 28 at the other end.

Special teams did the work: the Flyers went 3-for-5 on the power play and killed all four Canucks power plays. Jamie Oleksiak took three penalties on his own. The Flyers improved to 10-12-6, fifth in the Metropolitan, while the Canucks fell to 6-21-1, still last in the NHL.

items.text: The Canucks are on a three-game losing streak.
Christian Dvorak has a point in five straight games.
The Flyers have beaten the Canucks four straight times, going back to last season.
NHL.com had projected the Flyers with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
